sections.h2: Where does Owensboro fit in Kentucky's housing market?
sections.html:
Daviess County's seat is Owensboro, Kentucky's fourth most populous city, along U.S. 60 and Interstate 165 roughly 107 miles southwest of Louisville. The 2020 census counted 60,183 residents, and the Census Bureau estimated 60,892 on July 1, 2025, a rise of only 1.1 percent from the 2020 base. The wider metro area, which also takes in Hancock and McLean counties, was estimated at 116,506.

Census figures for 2020-2024 show 25,451 households, 57.4 percent of them owners, with a median home value of $178,900 and median gross rent of $905. Workers spend a mean of 17.1 minutes getting to their jobs.

sections.h2: What is the land and weather like around an Owensboro house?
sections.html:
The city sits in the crook of a bend in the Ohio River, 37 miles southeast of Evansville, Indiana. It covers 20.4 square miles, of which 6.47 percent is water. The settlement began as Yellow Banks, after the color of the bluffs beside the river, was formally established as Owensborough in 1817 and took its shorter modern spelling in 1893.

Summers run hot and sticky and winters are moderately cold. Storms, tornadoes among them, can arrive in most months. An F3 tornado cut through the city on December 9, 1952, so it is worth checking the roof and gutters for storm damage before a house is shown.

  • The city has 26,918 housing units, with 6.7 percent vacant in the 2020 census.
  • Owensboro Public Schools and Daviess County Public Schools both serve the area, along with the Catholic school system.
  • Brescia University, Kentucky Wesleyan College and Owensboro Community and Technical College are based in the city.

sections.h2: Which industries have supported Owensboro homeowners?
sections.html:
Owensboro has a long industrial past. Bourbon distilling, tobacco stemmeries, a wagon works, furniture and light bulb and vacuum tube plants all took turns as major employers, and two distilleries, Glenmore and Green River, are still in operation. A gas pipeline company moved its headquarters here in 1948, and a welding and steel tank firm founded on the riverfront in 1932 is now one of the country's largest suppliers of storage tanks.

sections.h2: What does Owensboro's population say about who buys here?
sections.html:
The median age in Owensboro was 38.1 in the 2020 census, and 18.3 percent of residents were 65 or older. The Census Bureau's newer estimate puts the share aged 65 and over at 19.0 percent. About 34.9 percent of households are made up of one person, and 14.9 percent are one person aged 65 or older, so a good share of sellers are older owners downsizing or heirs settling an estate.

Owners with a mortgage pay a median $1,321 a month in housing costs, those without one $522, and 85.3 percent of residents were in the same home a year before. The 2020 census counted 25,105 households, of which 29.0 percent had children under 18 at home.

The city carries some civic recognition: it was named an All-America City in 2013, and the Bluegrass Music Hall of Fame and Museum, which won a Governor's Award for Community Arts that year, sits on the riverfront. Evidence of Native American settlement here goes back 12,000 years, and the Ohio River riverfront park carries the name of the first European settler.

sections.h2: How does Owensboro enforce its property maintenance code?
sections.html:
The city enforces a Property Maintenance Code through Public Works. Ordinance 37-2019 amends the original 2011 ordinance and adopts provisions of the 2009 International Property Maintenance Code, and any violation counts as a nuisance. The code covers roughly 24,000 private parcels inside the city limits.

  • Code Enforcement Officers investigate, inspect and document conditions on a property.
  • A Notice of Violation comes first, with a citation after it.
  • Owners can appeal, and the city can abate a nuisance and enter property under the ordinance.

An empty or inherited house in poor shape should have its notices cleared before sale, or the buyer should be told what they cover. Cash buyers often take houses with deferred maintenance, since they plan the repairs themselves.

sections.h2: What does a seller owe at the Daviess County Clerk in Owensboro?
sections.html:
Owensboro deeds are recorded by the Daviess County Clerk, and the seller settles Kentucky's transfer tax there under KRS 142.050: $0.50 on each $500 of value, with a partial unit counting in full. A sale at the Census median of $178,900 owes $179.

A few transfers owe nothing, among them tax sales, partitions, divorce transfers between spouses, foreclosures and deeds in lieu. Call the clerk for the current recording fee, which can change, and ask the county PVA about your assessment and any exemption before you settle on a closing date.

sections.h2: When does a cash offer suit an Owensboro house?
sections.html:
Owensboro owners often hold older houses and face a small pool of showings, so a direct sale can save months. A cash buyer pays at closing and does not wait for a lender's appraisal, which helps when the roof, wiring or foundation needs work.

  • An estate where the owner has died or entered care and the family lives out of state.
  • A rental whose tenant left a damage list.
  • A property under a Property Maintenance notice the owner cannot afford to fix.
  • A move for work to Evansville, Louisville or elsewhere on a fixed date.

Request the offer in writing and ask who covers closing costs. Weigh the net against a listing after repairs, carrying costs and the transfer tax, and confirm any mortgage payoff with your lender.

sections.h2: Who runs Owensboro, and why does that matter to a seller?
sections.html:
Owensboro is a home rule city and has used a city manager form of government since 1954. Voters elect a mayor to a four-year term and four commissioners to two-year terms, and the commissioners hire a city manager who runs daily operations. Code, permit and utility questions therefore go to city departments, not to the commission directly.

If you want to sell fast, collect the paperwork the buyer will want: the deed, any recorded liens, recent tax bills and notices from Code Enforcement. A clear file moves a sale to closing sooner whether the buyer pays cash or uses a lender.

faqs.q: What tax applies when an Owensboro house sells?
faqs.a: Kentucky's transfer tax, paid by the seller at $0.50 per $500 of value. At Owensboro's $178,900 median that is $179 after rounding the partial unit up.

faqs.q: Who enforces upkeep standards in Owensboro?
faqs.a: Code Enforcement Officers under the city's Public Works department inspect, issue notices of violation and citations, and can abate nuisances.

faqs.q: Can an Owensboro house with a violation notice be sold?
faqs.a: Yes. Read the notice, note the fix or appeal deadline and disclose it to the buyer. A cash buyer may take on the repair after closing.
The Daviess County Clerk, since the county records land for all its cities. Ask for the current recording fee before closing.
